summary: Narrow recheck of the integration-discovered PostgreSQL snapshot-order correction completed. Sorting the top-level entity collections and member list removes incidental row-order dependence while retaining binding to record contents, nested array order, membership, and tenant identity. No supported token-binding regression identified.
coverage: Inspected records()/identity()/compareId(), snapshot collection normalization, member normalization, canonical() and final proposal/batch token inputs. Sorting maps the collection to a new array, preserves every record, and does not recurse into payload/content/check arrays. Existing persisted state and entity storage keys establish stable unique nodeId/id identities; membership rows are unique per tenant/user. The workspace object and all nested fields remain in the digest.

Inspected the backend-independent single/batch reversed-state-list regressions and existing stale-target/proposal checks. Read the worker-produced .check/proposal-order-debug/{before-fix,diagnosis,after-fix}.json artifacts: the index/sequential scan pair has matching sorted before-state digests; tokensEqual changes from false before correction to true after correction. These PostgreSQL artifacts were inspected, not independently executed by this reviewer.

Executed node .check/independent-review/order-binding-recheck.ts, which imports the actual buildProposalPreview and uses isolated in-memory dependency stubs without a database. All 14 assertions passed: each of six entity collection permutations and member permutation preserves the token; check steps, evidence observation arrays, task checklist order, member names, record values, record membership, and tenant identity remain token-sensitive. Output is .check/independent-review/order-binding-recheck-output.json.
limitations: This is a focused follow-up informed by the integration regression and proposed fix, not a new independent first pass. The two original review findings and their earlier corrections remain recorded separately.

The 14-case reviewer check exercises actual token construction with isolated dependency stubs; it does not execute database transactions. PostgreSQL plan switching and both-backend proposal suites were performed by the implementation worker, with final integration checks owned by the lead. No browser, build, full-suite, or product source edits were performed during this follow-up.
